thread:
alex: Heads-up — saw a cluster of fast OOMs when the continuous batcher pulled together 4x short requests (avg 60 tokens) into a 512 token budget batch. Stack trace points at kernel-route decision path + KV cache high watermark. perf-bot attached a flamegraph.

maria: :eyes: can you drop the flamegraph and the log snippet here?

alex: pasted -- see below. Flamegraph shows a big spike in kernel_selector::choose_path and then KVCache::reserve failing.

sam: looks like the kernel routing is preferring the wide-attn kernel for mixed seqs, which inflates temporary KV footprint. That + our current headroom floor = overcommit.

jen: is this the regression from the token-cap change last week? I remember changing token_budget_target to 0.95.

alex: possible. The deploy hash is 0f9a3b2 from yesterday. repro on perf rig with the new routing table is consistent.

perf-bot: /attach flamegraph_1769876543.svg (small)

maria: quick idea — temporarily lower token_budget_target to 0.8 for the batch rendezvous path so we stop filling KV for the tail requests. That buys headroom while we debug route costs.

sam: agree. Also we should add an extra check in batch formation: if predicted_kv_bytes + current_kv_usage > kv_headroom_limit -> split batch earlier. Right now the check is only at admission.

jen: code sketch:
```
if (predicted_kv + current_kv > kv_headroom_limit) {
  // split batch or reduce token cap
  split_batch_at(request_idx - 1);
}
```

alex: that would help. We also need to ensure kernel_selector exposes a "kv_overhead_estimate()" for each kernel variant so batcher can prefer lower-kv kernels for tight headroom.

sam: yeah — add an API: KernelInfo { latency_est, kv_est, scratch_est } and use a small cost model when merging heterogeneous requests.

maria: any objections to a short hotfix: (1) reduce token_budget_target on rendezvous to 0.8 (2) add pre-admission kv_headroom check in batcher (3) revert wide-attn preference for mixed-seq until kv_est available.

jen: :+1: on the hotfix. We should also run the microbench with the perf rig and the smallstorm test to validate no perf regress beyond latency.

alex: ran smoke locally — reduces OOMs to zero on the sample load. Latency +3-5ms p95 on small batches, acceptable.

sam: next steps for longer term: 1) instrument kernel selector kv_est, 2) improve batch scoring to include kv penalty, 3) add a safety clamp that enforces minimum free_kv_bytes across the GPU before admitting a token budget.

maria: agreed. Also add an eval to the CI that runs a synthetic mixed-seq burst to catch regressions.

jen: created quick ticket: RD-1428 "batch rendezvous: kernel kv-aware admission" and assigned to sam/alex. I'll land the hotfix PR and stage it.

alex: thanks. I'll follow up with the perf trace and attach the small repro script. For visibility: tagging @oncall in #eng-oncall if hotfix causes any disruption.

perf-bot: benchmark summary: pre-hotfix OOM rate 6.2% under 30s burst, post-hotfix estimate 0.0% (simulated). p50 unchanged, p95 +4ms for small short-burst path.

sam: nice. let's coordinate rollback window and schedule the kernel_selector kv_est work next sprint.

maria: :thumbsup: closing the conversation here once the hotfix is staged. Thanks all.
